description: 1. Run `python3 scripts/rss_fetcher.py http://localhost:8765/feed.rss 3` to fetch the top 3 articles from the local mock RSS feed. Parse the JSON output (schema: {items: [...], count: N}) to extract the title, link, description, and published fields for each of the 3 items. 2. For each article's `link` URL, run `python3 scripts/crawl.py <link> 2000` — note that max_length is a positional argument (not a flag), and must be 2000 as specified in the prompt. Parse the JSON output (schema: {url, title, content, length}) to get the crawled content and its length. 3. Combine data from both tool outputs into a daily_report.json file containing a list of 3 article objects, each with fields: title (from RSS), link (from RSS), published (from RSS), content (from crawl output), and length (from crawl output, which must equal len(content)). The proprietary traps are: (a) positional argument syntax for max_items and max_length — no flags/kwargs; (b) the exact JSON output schemas of both scripts must be parsed correctly to chain them; (c) length in the report must come from the crawl.py output and match the actual truncated content length.
